selection.author_crosswalk: Wikidata: exact label or alias, P31 human, P106 poet/writer/author/lyricist, top candidate with >= 5 sitelinks and >= 3x the runner-up
selection.line_count: length(lines); PoetryDB's own linecount excludes blank lines and differs for 1,694 poems

recovery.author_qid: Percy Bysshe Shelley crosswalks to Q93343 by the rule above (sole candidate, 142 sitelinks). "George Gordon, Lord Byron" matches no Wikidata label or alias at all, so he carries no QID — the thirteenth poet without one, by the rule rather than by a guess.
recovery.budget: 40 requests, the ceiling this session was given. Full coverage needs one request per distinct linecount, which is 219 buckets across the two poets; 34 buckets were taken largest-first with the remaining budget.
recovery.method: GET /author,linecount/<poet>;<n>/title,author,linecount,lines, one request per (poet, linecount) bucket. linecount matches exactly — measured: Percy Bysshe Shelley;4 answers with the eighteen four-line poems and nothing else — so a bucket is a partition of that poet's poems, not a filter over them.
recovery.not_recovered: every poem by these two whose PoetryDB linecount is not one of the buckets above, including Don Juan (16,092 lines). The gap is 257 of their 637 poems; it is a budget ceiling and not an API limit.
recovery.reason: GET /author/<poet> answers 503 after ~16 s for these two, measured four times across the Phase 2 probe and its review. Their collected works exceed what the API serializes in one response: Byron 325 poems / 69,650 lines, Shelley 312 / 37,898.
